method: We reviewed u12.json at commit db23058 (02:27 UTC). The file is byte-identical at HEAD 4c94af4 (md5 d592e4e6…). The rule-cards and lexicon owners committed their round-3 wave while we worked: rule-cards db87d27 at 02:32, lexicon 784cc65, f0ddb3f and b2b9a39 between 02:34 and 02:38. Everything below reflects those files as they stand at HEAD 4c94af4, which we re-read at 02:40 UTC. Both reviewers read every German string of the unit again. That covered title and title.canDo, the Folge (9 lines, 2 glosses) and its gist item, and the three inputs: the LS1 class dialogue, the LS2 web page with 10 lines (ls2-l10 now carries the hotel Praktikum and the „Hotel“ gloss), and the LS3 e-mail with the office scene. It also covered the 9 LS4 texts, both strategy cards, the 8 redemittel with their function labels, both Aussprache blocks, the three rule cards the unit shows (rc.perfekt-sein, rc.wollen, rc.verbposition-2), the Sp1+Sp2 task (instructions, situations, cards, persona, openingLine, 8 hintWords, 16 model turns) and the S2 task (situation, taskDe, 3 Leitpunkte, checklist, 33-word model). Finally we read the Fokus card, the fact record, story beat and cliffhanger, every endLine, promptDe, option and explanation.de, and the 24 u12 word cards in a1.1/lexicon.json. We solved all 102 authored items blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line: start gist 1, input 15, structured input 12, pool 33, reserve 15, perception 8, exam 9, check 8 and proof 1. That includes the six gist and detail items whose distractors the author replaced beyond r2's request (ls1-i01, ls2-i01 to ls2-i04, ls3-i01). A script graded every answer and accepted form with the real grader, src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js. All 231 answer and accepted strings (each accepted list repeats its key) grade CORRECT. The non-exam three-option keys sit at 11 / 11 / 13. We ran 78 further candidate answers through checkItem. They cover person endings, the wollen stem vowel, the anfangen umlaut, sein and haben forms, number echoes, every correction's unchanged quoted sentence and dictation slips; the results are quoted in F02, F04 and notes. We compiled a1.1 into the scratchpad (node scripts/course-v2/compile.mjs a1.1 --out <scratch> --banks-out <scratch>), so nothing was written to the repo. We then ran normalizeSpeakingTask and buildCoursePartnerPrompt({ level: 'a1.1', task }) of netlify/functions/_shared/speakingAI.mjs on the compiled a11-u12-s entry (F01). We scanned every German string against knownForms(a1.1, 12) from scripts/course-v2/lib-validate/lexicon.mjs. That scan included the surfaces the validator does not walk: the Fokus card, the redemittel labels, the story beat, the cliffhanger and the persona (F05). We checked exam fidelity against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json (h2, l3, sp1, sp2, s2). We checked cast and story against casts/series.json, casts/a1.json and u01–u11. To size the paradigm class, we compared the A1.1 verbs whose lexicon Perfekt is „ist …“ against rc.perfekt-sein (F06), and we compared the owner files' last commits with the r2 date.

verdict: Not exit-ready: 1 BLOCKER, 1 MAJOR, 5 MINOR. None of them is owned by the unit. The unit author landed every unit-side fix r2 asked for, each as proposed. l3-02 is now decided by the sign and its location. ls1-i04's options are all heard, Arta says „dort“, the du-form carries ls2-s01, the Fokus title and body lost their B1 words, and ls2-l10 sets up the hotel Praktikum. The author also cleaned six gist and detail items of unheard distractors, and all six are sound. The rule-cards owner closed r2-F03 while we reviewed: rc.verbposition-2 now models „Was lernen Sie?“. The German is correct on every model surface. All 102 keys and all 231 answer and accepted strings grade correct, and H2, L3, Sp1, Sp2 and S2 are exact to sd1.json with original tasks. Two points stop exit, and neither is in u12.json. (1) F01, BLOCKER, E1 server track: the speaking engine still drops `parts`, so the Teil 2 card round that proves cd.a1.lernziele and cd.a1.herkunft-situation is neither run nor scored. (2) F02, MAJOR, checker owner, new in this unit's trail. r1 and r2 tested orders, W-words and numbers, not verb forms. The grader calls the target errors of the unit's new spine point typos. „wollst“ for „willst“, „willen“ for „wollen“, „willt“ and „wollst“ for „wollt“, and „fangt“ and „fängst“ for „fängt“ all pass after one retry. That is the class of u03 r3-F01, u08 r3-F03 and u10 r3-F03. The five minors are all held by owners: receptive Monat and Jahr (lexicon owner), the number echo in two gaps (checker owner), the Fokus card's unglossed words (SCHEMA owner and rule-smith), rc.perfekt-sein (rule-cards owner) and three word cards plus mitmachen (lexicon owner). findings.problem: This class is new in u12's trail. r1 and r2 tested orders, W-words, numbers and names, not verb forms. r2 even recorded „Wann fangt der Kurs an?“ → typo without flagging it. a1.1-u03 r3-F01 found the class after our r2, and u08 r3-F03 and u10 r3-F03 confirmed it. check.js calls a one-letter difference a typo unless the last letter changes. g.wollen is this unit's new productive spine point, and its paradigm is exactly such inner differences: the stem alternation will-/woll- and the endings -st/-t. That is what rc.wollen tables. So on three of the four typed pool items for wollen, the typical learner errors come back TYPO: the o-stem in the singular („wollst“), the i-stem in the plural („willen“, „willt“), and the wrong person ending („wollst“ for ihr). ItemView gives one retry and then logs the unchanged answer as correct. The same holds for the Vokalwechsel and the ending of anfangen in ls3-p04 and ls3-p10, whose promptEn asks for „er-form“. The scored Check is safe here (c02 key „will“: „wollt“ and „willt“ → wrong), and the corrections' unchanged quoted sentences grade wrong because their errors are word order. The misses also reach no repair card. ls2-p01 to ls2-p04 and c02 carry no errorTag, because SCHEMA's ErrorTag enum has no verb-ending tag (u01 r3-F10), so check.js tags them „Rechtschreibung“ or „Wortschatz“. A grader that accepts the error an item exists to remove is a gate hole (§9.4 MAJOR). The class stands in at least nine a1.1 units (u03 r3-F01 scan) and has no rule, so it is stop-the-line. The unit cannot fix it: CLAUDE.md puts the rule in the checker, never in accepted[], and there is no item field for known wrong forms.
findings.fix: Checker owner, as u03 r3-F01, in the v2 wrapper src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js so that the live course's grading is untouched. (1) A typed single-token item whose topic is a v2 spine id (/^g\./) is graded strictly. The ae/oe/ue and ss folds stay („faengt“ stays CORRECT), and a case-only slip stays TYPO. (2) An edit within the last two letters is an ending change, never a typo. (3) Extend u03's stem-vowel rule to the modal alternation: the key's paradigm twin (will- ↔ woll-, and likewise kann- ↔ könn-, muss- ↔ müss-) grades WRONG, as the umlaut twin of a Vokalwechsel verb does (fangt ↔ fängt). A genuine slip such as „wilst“ stays TYPO. SCHEMA owner: add the verb-ending ErrorTag (u01 r3-F10). The unit author then tags ls2-p01 to ls2-p04, ls2-r01, ls2-r05 and c02 with it. Unit: no edit until that tag exists.

Checked and not raised. (1) q01 „Im Buch steht: „Lesen Sie den Text. Kreuzen Sie dann an.“ Was machen Sie am Ende?“ can be solved by taking the last-mentioned step once „am Ende“ is understood; „dann“ adds nothing because mention order equals action order. That is the same demand as the approved exemplar's q02 (find „Zucker“, take its price), and it still needs German (am Ende, and ankreuzen against schreiben), so we accept it. If the owner wants „dann/zuerst“ to decide, the inverted order „Kreuzen Sie an. Aber lesen Sie zuerst den Text.“ with the same question would do it. (2) ls1-p10 and ls1-r04 reject a correction that also fronts a phrase („Nach Leipzig bin ich geflogen.“ → wrong). The prompt asks „haben oder sein?“, so the minimal correction is the right key, as u10 r3 ruled for its ls2-p10. (3) ls3-p02 grades „Wieviel“ CORRECT because the item lists it, which endorses the pre-1996 spelling; „wieviel“ grades TYPO. The cleaner fix is a checker TYPO for a missing space, not a listed variant. The LEX-03 advisory on it is noise. (4) ls2-l10 „Jetzt will ich die Prüfung machen. Dann will ich wieder am Empfang arbeiten. Aber zuerst will ich ein Praktikum in einem Hotel machen.“ is natural spoken German: „zuerst“ scopes over the job just named. This is our own r2 wording, and the author added „Aber“. (5) The Sp1 situation adds „Sagen Sie auch: Seit wann lernen Sie Deutsch?“ to the seven SD1 keywords. sd1.sp1 says not all keywords are needed and candidates may say more, the model turns include it, and it trains no wrong exam behaviour. (7) „Bringen Sie den Teil pünktlich zurück.“: „Abschnitt abgeben“ is the term, but „Teil“ was our r2 wording to stay within the level and is clear on an optional card.
